content.Title: Retrieval-augmented generation for production systems
content.Subtitle: How to combine search with language models
content.Content:
Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) combines a retriever with a language model. The retriever finds relevant documents from a knowledge base. The language model then uses those documents as context when writing an answer. Vector databases store embeddings so similar passages can be found quickly. This pattern is useful when you want answers grounded in your own data instead of only the model's training set.

A typical RAG pipeline has four stages: ingest source documents, split them into chunks, embed each chunk, and store the vectors. At query time you embed the question, retrieve the nearest chunks, and pass them to the model as context. Reranking can improve quality by scoring the retrieved passages with a cross-encoder before generation.
